title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, a $1/$5 per-million-token computer-use model (Oct 26)
bullets.summary: Mid-tier model aimed at computer use, priced 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, available in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API as gpt-6.1-terra; Signal Drift reports it finishes tasks 3x faster than GPT-6 Astra (secondary write-up, OpenAI page not retrieved).
bullets.how: The Construct: a cheap benchmark candidate for high-volume browser/computer-use routines; test against current models before switching. PRAGMA: cost anchor for client agent budgets. Brand 9 Signs: maybe for supplier-portal automation like Signs365 order runs.

bullets.title: Claude Mythos/Fable 5.5 still unconfirmed; a Mythos 5.5 mention surfaced on Anthropic's Mythos page (Nov 1)
bullets.summary: TestingCatalog reports a 'Claude Mythos 5.5' label with no specs or announcement and anecdotal A/B tests of Fable 5.5 checkpoints; kingy.ai's tracker (updated Nov 3) says the latest confirmed Fable is 5.1 and the 5.5 LiteLLM entry is a catalog artifact. Launch timing is speculation.
bullets.how: The Construct: no action until Anthropic announces; keep model IDs configurable so a new tier can be benchmarked on release day. PRAGMA: don't promise clients a specific new model.

bullets.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, gated to cyber defenders, tops Artificial Analysis index at 59 (Oct 28)
bullets.summary: Frontier model for long-horizon engineering and cyber defense, access starting with a small defender group and no general-availability date; intro API price $2/$10 per million tokens rising to $4/$20; Signal Drift cites it ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and GPT-6 Astra (57).
bullets.how: The Construct: not usable yet; watch for general availability as a benchmark rival. PRAGMA: shows frontier labs gating the strongest models, so client plans should assume tiered access.

bullets.title: Mistral publishes Mistral Large 4 open weights, ~1T parameters / 49B active (Oct 29)
bullets.summary: Modified-MIT license (hosted-service use needs a commercial license), Mistral API at $0.70/$2.10 per million tokens; Mistral claims open-model leadership in coding and defensive security while Vals AI ranks it 17th of 30 overall.
bullets.how: The Construct: an option for a self-hosted or low-cost worker tier, but too large for casual local runs; license matters for PRAGMA client hosting. Brand 9 Signs: no.

bullets.title: GitHub: AI agents wrote the first draft of 40%+ of pull requests in September, up from 17% in March (reported Oct 28)
bullets.summary: GitHub's own figures as relayed by Signal Drift's weekly roundup; the same roundup notes Anthropic's SEC IPO filing (Nasdaq: ANT) on Oct 26.
bullets.how: The Construct: validates agent-authored code as the norm, so invest in review gates and tests over authorship. PRAGMA: usable adoption stat in client pitches. Brand 9 Signs: indirect.

praxis_lesson: Capability and price tiers shift weekly (a $1/$5 computer-use model, a gated frontier model, a trillion-parameter open-weights release), so route each routine to the cheapest tier that passes its own test and keep model IDs in config, not code. (Quiet day: no verified new MCP servers in video/CRM/DAM/signage; the Pictory/WellSaid video-voice MCPs surfaced are older; several items are 2-9 days old and rest on aggregator write-ups.)
